why: The dominant design -- real temp git repos, real subprocess/importlib against the actual scripts, no mocks -- is correct for dev-tooling oracles and should not be replaced. The one real opening is Hypothesis on the safety_gate denylist and codemap escaper, free since it already resolves through the sibling env. pytest-randomly/xdist are reasonable but blocked on this dir having no dependency manifest of its own.

alternatives.name: hypothesis
alternatives.covers: Importable today at zero new cost: already resolves via the sibling intent-control-plane env (verified: `uv run --project intent-control-plane python -m pytest tests/ -q` -> 57 passed).
alternatives.gap: Unused here. test_mastery_controls.py:434 hand-picks 13 literal shell commands vs safety_gate.py's 18-rule regex denylist; test_codemap.py:144 checks table-escaping with a couple examples, not a roundtrip property.
alternatives.cost: Free; effectively already paid for via the sibling project.
alternatives.maturity: Mature; already trusted elsewhere in this repo.

alternatives.name: pytest-xdist / pytest-randomly
alternatives.covers: CPU parallelism + order randomization; suite is parallel-safe (each case uses its own tempdir/mkdtemp).
alternatives.gap: Not installed. 44.92s for 59 tests locally; 2 of 3 files are subprocess/git-heavy, the slowest in the repo.
alternatives.cost: Free, but no root pyproject.toml/requirements.txt exists to declare it in.
alternatives.maturity: xdist v3.8.0, randomly v4.1.0, both active pytest-dev projects.

alternatives.name: schemathesis
alternatives.covers: Fuzzes an HTTP/GraphQL API from its schema.
alternatives.gap: Everything: every subject script (hooks, codemap.py, gate.py, knowledge.py) is CLI/stdin-JSON, not a served API with a schema.
alternatives.maturity: PyPI v4.24.2, maintained, wrong tool class.

alternatives.name: testcontainers
alternatives.covers: Real disposable service containers in Docker for integration tests.
alternatives.gap: Everything: the closest 'external service' tested is real git via subprocess against tempdirs, already exercised directly -- no Docker need.
alternatives.cost: N/A; adds a Docker dependency this repo doesn't otherwise need.
alternatives.maturity: PyPI v4.15.0 (2026-07-24), very active, wrong class here.

alternatives.name: freezegun / syrupy
alternatives.gap: No datetime/time assertions found in this dir's tests; no under-asserted large generated output identified here (unlike the sibling project's dashboard render).
alternatives.maturity: freezegun v1.5.5, syrupy v5.5.3, both maintained.

evidence: Read test_mastery_controls.py in full, test_codemap.py lines 1-120, safety_gate.py in full, test_gate_extra_domains.py in full. wc -l showed 870 then 1176 lines as a 3rd file appeared live. Ran pytest via sibling env: 57 passed, 2 failed (unrelated prior-art gap in tools/map). Confirmed no root pyproject.toml via ls.
recheck: uv run --project intent-control-plane python -m pytest ../tests -q; wc -l tests/*.py; ls for a root pyproject.toml added since.
migration_loc: +60/-25 Hypothesis grammar test replaces 13-line tuple (test_mastery_controls.py:435-449); +10/-5 codemap escaper roundtrip. xdist/randomly need a root pyproject.toml first.
what_ours_does: unittest.TestCase oracle suite for this repo's own dev-tooling scripts. Measured 494 lines at dispatch (= test_mastery_controls.py alone). Mid-audit a 3rd file (test_gate_extra_domains.py, 306 lines) appeared live, growing the dir to 1176 lines -- an active background pipeline touches this repo. Drives hooks/tools via importlib or real subprocess (JSON stdin) and real temp git repos, no mocks.
strongest_counterargument: These are oracle tests proving a real script makes a real decision; mocking or fuzzing over them changes what is being proven. safety_gate.py's own docstring says the regex denylist is 'not an OS security boundary,' so hardening its test proves a marginally better regex, not a safe guardrail -- effort a one-person maintainer may reasonably spend elsewhere.
